title: What Questions Should I Ask Before Hiring an Architect in Westchester NY
excerpt: Choosing the right architect for your Westchester home project is one of the most important decisions you'll make. Here are the questions you should ask to make sure you're hiring someone who can actually deliver.
content:
When you're planning a renovation, addition, or new construction project in Westchester, you need an architect who understands your home and your vision. But not every architect is the same, and asking the right questions upfront can save you time, money, and headaches down the road.

Whether you're in Scarsdale, Mamaroneck, or Pelham, the process starts with a conversation. Here's what you should know before you hire.

Is This Person Actually Licensed to Do the Work?

This is the first question, and it matters more than you'd think. Ask if the architect is a licensed architect in New York. Not just someone who designs homes, but someone who holds an actual license from the New York State Department of State. That credential means they've passed exams, met education requirements, and are held accountable to professional standards.

Next, find out if they're also a general contractor. This is rarer, but valuable. If your architect in Westchester also carries a general contractor license, they understand both sides of construction. They know what contractors face in the field. They know realistic timelines and what actually works when you're building. Silvio M. Luca, principal of House Architecture & Construction, holds both licenses. He runs every project personally, which means your design work and construction work are guided by one person who understands the complete picture.

Will They Actually Manage Your Project From Start to Finish?

Some architects hand off their work to junior staff once the design is done. Ask who will be managing your project. Will the architect you hired be the one checking in with you, reviewing progress, and solving problems? Or will you be working with someone else once construction starts?

When you're planning a home renovation in Westchester NY, this matters. You want the same person who understood your vision during design to be there when questions come up during construction. Whether you're doing a kitchen remodel in White Plains, a second-story addition in Larchmont, or a primary suite addition in Bronxville, consistency matters.

Do They Know the Permit Process in Your Town?

Every municipality in Westchester has its own building department and permit process. Hastings-on-Hudson has its own process. So does Rye. So does Tarrytown. It's normal for each town to have different requirements, timelines, and standards.

Ask your architect if they've worked in your specific town before. Have they managed permit applications there? Do they know the local building inspector? Do they understand what that particular municipality expects? Experience matters here, because a delay in permitting can push your entire timeline back.

What Services Do They Actually Offer?

Make sure the architect you're considering can handle the type of project you need. If you're thinking about an open-concept conversion, kitchen remodel, historic restoration, or custom new construction, ask if they've done that work before. If you want to add a second story to your home in Harrison, ask if they've tackled second-story additions. A good architect should be honest about what they do well and what falls outside their wheelhouse.

Hiring a residential architect in Scarsdale or any other Westchester community means finding someone who listens, who holds the right licenses, and who will be there to manage your project from start to finish.
